summary: Intermittent initial-token stall on chat completions observed after runtime micro-patch and model handoff
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent long delays before the first token (initial-token stall) for chat completions after we rolled a small runtime micro-patch and enabled a model handoff policy that favors quantized variants during high load.

Impact: Several live chat sessions for AtlasHealth experienced 3-6 second stalls before the first token; downstream UX shows spinning indicator and some clients timed out at 10s. Estimated ~12% of chat requests to their tenant in us-east-1 during the incident window were impacted.

Environment: production (us-east-1), customer on dedicated/reserved capacity with routing policy that pins to preferred variants. A runtime micro-patch (runtime v1.5.3->v1.5.4) and routing config (enable-quant-handoff=true) were applied earlier in the morning.

Steps to reproduce (how customer reproduced):
1) Open long-lived chat session with model pinned to llama-3-70b-instruct on AtlasHealth tenant.
2) Send a multi-turn user prompt that triggers tool-calling/structured output path.
3) Observe initial token delay ~3-6s intermittently (not every request).

Observed behavior: Initial token emission delayed despite downstream token generation continuing normally once tokens start; CPU/GPU utilization normal for serving node. Streaming connection remains open then starts streaming after the stall. No 5xx errors returned.

Expected behavior: First token should be emitted within ~300-800ms for this customer workload given dedicated capacity SLA.

Attached logs/samples: Provided request ids in customer report: req_us_east_20260311_0212_a3c2, req_us_east_20260311_0225_b8f4. Traces showed long gap between router->executor queue dequeue and first kernel invocation on a subset of requests.

investigation_notes:
Timeline: 07:45 UTC runtime v1.5.4 micro-patch + enable-quant-handoff flag; customer complaints start ~08:10 UTC.
Telemetry: Per-request traces indicate an elevated scheduling delay between router handoff and executor launch on ~12% of requests; kernel invocation time unchanged. CPU/GPU utilization normal; queuing observed on specific executor pool instances serving quantized variants.
Repro steps executed on staging with synthetic load reproduced the initial-token stall only when routing policy switched in-flight to quantized variants and KV cache was cold. Adding a cache-warm reduced stalls.
Hypothesis: The quantized-serving path triggers a slow codepath on the first sequence (cold paths for int8 kernel selection + extra prefix conversion), combined with a routing handoff that causes a short scheduling pause. Subsequent tokens benefit from warmed KV/cache and faster kernels.
Tests run: rollback routing, cache warm, single-node isolation, add micro-benchmark for quantized kernel cold-start. Results: rollback + warm restores TTFB; kernel cold-start measurable ~2.4s overhead in worst case on affected hardware when combined with routing switch.
resolution:
Root cause: interaction between the new model handoff policy (quantized variant selection) and the runtime's quantized kernel cold-start path produced intermittent scheduling and conversion overheads that manifested as initial-token stalls.
Fix applied: 1) Immediate rollback of handoff flag for AtlasHealth tenant at 2026-03-12 00:48 UTC. 2) Deployed targeted cache-warm and preflight kernel selection on affected pools (hotfix in runtime PR #3421). 3) Added a short GC/warmup hook in routing to avoid mid-request handoffs to cold quantized instances.
Verification: Post-fix telemetry shows median initial-token latency returned to baseline (from p50~1.8s during incident to p50~0.55s after fix) and timeout rates dropped to near zero for customer. Customer validated UX improvement and closed their blocking ticket.
postmortem_action_items: Add regression test for model handoff -> quantized variant cold-start in nightly e2e suite
Instrument per-variant kernel cold-start metrics and alert if >500ms increased p95 for first-token
Change default handoff policy to prefer warmed pools or perform transparent background warming before switching traffic
Update rollout checklist: include cache-warm and kernel-warm steps when enabling quantized-handoff in prod
Follow up with runtime team PR #3421 to harden cold-start path and reduce conversion overhead
